name: What's the difference between a Junior ADU and a standard ADU?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a Junior ADU and a standard ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main differences between a Junior ADU (JADU) and a standard ADU lie in their size, location, and utility requirements. A JADU is limited to 500 square feet, must be contained within the existing footprint of a single-family home, and requires an efficiency kitchen. It also does not typically require new utility connections. A standard ADU can be larger, up to 1,200 square feet (depending on jurisdiction), can be attached or detached, and often requires separate utility hookups and parking. JADUs are generally a simpler and more cost-effective option for adding housing.
acceptedAnswer.description: A JADU is up to 500 sq ft within an existing home with an efficiency kitchen; a standard ADU can be larger, attached or detached, and may require separate utilities.
